title: The Enlightened Society of the Weeping Moon
summary: America's leading secret society of the age.

claims.text: Among America's many secret societies the foremost is the Enlightened Society of the Weeping Moon.
It has much in common with Freemasonry and almost surely grew from it; like the Masons it keeps its rites and business from outsiders.

title: Glastonbury Tor
summary: A thaumaturgical focus the Tremere guard.

claims.text: The castle on the Tor remains a strong thaumaturgical focus, and the local Tremere guard it closely in hope of tapping its power.
After Arthur's grave was found in the 1100s, stones from the castle went into building the Church of St. Michael on the Tor.

title: Strasbourg
summary: A free city for Kindred travellers.

claims.text: Kindred treat Strasbourg as a handy starting point for almost anywhere in Western Europe.
Its primogen keep the old garrison town free for travellers who can pay their way and are wise enough not to make trouble, using the resented mortal government as cover.

title: Victoria's Royal Web
summary: How the queen's family ties tangle the Kindred of Europe.

claims.text: Queen Victoria's grandchildren married into most of Europe's royal houses, from Russia, Germany and Spain to Scandinavia, the Balkans and the old Bourbon-Orleans line of France.
These ties keep throwing together Kindred from across Europe who would otherwise have little in common, and the friction that follows is constant.
The end of Reconstruction in 1877 eased the city's burdens but left behind a group of Kindred from the North who had tasted power there and want more.
These newcomers, mostly Ventrue, are based in the American Quarter and work out of the St. Charles Hotel.
The United States, relying on the Monroe Doctrine, loomed over a battered Mexico as the Colossus of the North, while rival leaders inside the country extorted tribute.

The Passaglia, a merchant family within the Giovanni who arrived with Marco Polo's expedition, are the classic example of Kindred who crossed into Asia early.
The Passaglia, and the Giovanni in general, credit their success in Asia to standing outside the Camarilla.

title: Kindred and the Interior of Africa
summary: Why most Kindred ignored the heart of the continent.

claims.text: Traders in gold, ivory and slaves mostly kept to coastal posts and waited for native middlemen to bring goods to them.
Most Kindred cared even less for the African interior, being busy holding on to their European domains.
